correctness.rationale: The event is exactly the pair of independent strip inequalities on the orthographic viewing slope. The equilateral normals classify the intersection as triangular for height ratios at least two and otherwise six-sided. The outward cone facet normals give three or six equal geodesic spherical turning angles, yielding the formulas by spherical Gauss–Bonnet; no sampling assumption enters these derivations. Fixed-sum optimizer follows from strict nesting in the triangular regime and the strictly positive derivative (6+8s²−24p)/(1+4s²−8p+16p²)^(3/2) in the hexagonal regime with p≤s²/4. At a=b=h the analytic Taylor expansion yields the explicit positive second-order coefficient. A pure-stdlib checker separately constructs projected vertices (1,260,000 views), integrates the slope density and checks the fixed-sum ordering; these only corroborate the theorem.

value.rationale: Simultaneous nonvisibility of the distinguished apices is a natural, nontrivial joint geometric statistic for the smallest bipyramid. The result solves an unrestricted positive two-height family exactly, reveals a sharp change from a triangular to a six-sided admissible-viewing cone at height ratio two, uniquely optimizes the event at fixed total height, and provides a positive sharp quadratic stability law. It is not merely a symmetric-special-case computation and yields a geometrically explanatory phase diagram.
